findings.title: Unmigrated section-access names still authorize users
findings.evidence: Authorization/GroupAuthorizationHandler.cs:74-76 reads dynamic section groups from SectionAccessService, then succeeds on GroupMembershipChecker at Authorization/GroupAuthorizationHandler.cs:92-96 or on user.IsInRole(allowedGroup) at Authorization/GroupAuthorizationHandler.cs:106-109 without first requiring allowedGroup to be a SID. GroupMembershipChecker also includes ClaimTypes.Role in extracted claims at Authorization/GroupMembershipChecker.cs:31-35 and exact-matches allowed values at Authorization/GroupMembershipChecker.cs:87-88. Trigger: a deferred/halted migration leaves section_access.group_value as a legacy name such as "ExchangeWebAdmins" (Services/SectionAccessSidMigration.cs:92-110), and the principal has a role claim or Windows token role for that name.
findings.predicted_failure: The user is granted access to the module based on a group name rather than the resolved SID, so same-named group/domain ambiguity remains live instead of failing closed. This is HIGH because the authorization table can still grant privileged module access to the wrong authorization subject whenever the SID migration is incomplete.

findings.title: Startup SID migration skips legacy file-backed section access
findings.evidence: Program.cs:223-224 runs SectionAccessSidMigration during startup, but the legacy config\sectionaccess.json import only runs in the SectionAccessService constructor at Services/SectionAccessService.cs:35-36. SectionAccessService is only registered at Program.cs:83 and is not resolved before the migration in this startup block. Trigger: upgrade with an empty SQLite section_access table and an existing config\sectionaccess.json; SectionAccessSidMigration sees zero rows and returns AlreadyMigrated at Services/SectionAccessSidMigration.cs:81-84.
findings.predicted_failure: The first later construction of SectionAccessService imports and archives the legacy name rows after the SID migration has already run. Until another restart, the authorization table contains names instead of SIDs; with the current handler that keeps name-based access open, and with a fail-closed SID-only handler it would deny legitimate configured users for that process lifetime. This is MEDIUM because a normal legacy upgrade path leaves the auth table in the pre-migration identity model until manual restart.
